🔥 key-caster | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To visually display keystrokes on-screen for Linux users, particularly useful for screen recording, live streaming, or demonstrating keyboard usage.
✨ Key Features: • Lightweight on-screen keystroke displayer • Supports Wayland, COSMIC, and X11 • Non-root execution via input group • Per-device hardware layout routing • Robust device hotplugging
📖 Summary: Key-caster is a lightweight, on-screen keystroke displayer for Linux that shows your key presses visually. It's designed to be unobtrusive and works across Wayland, COSMIC, and X11 environments, offering features like configuration persistence and privacy controls.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 murces | Java
🎯 Primary Use Case: Managing dedicated Minecraft servers on Linux/WSL2 environments, especially on resource-constrained systems like VPS or homelabs, by providing a lightweight, feature-rich terminal-based interface.
✨ Key Features: • Native Ahead-of-Time (AOT) Binary via GraalVM Native Image for fast startup and low memory usage • Portable OpenJDK Provisioning for on-demand Java runtime downloads
📖 Summary: MurCes is a high-performance, zero-overhead TUI and CLI manager for dedicated Minecraft servers on Linux and WSL2. It offers a lightweight alternative to heavy web panels, providing features like native binary compilation, detached process supervision, integrated mod management, safe world backups, and zero-config port forwarding.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 AutoMagik | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To automate the launching of specific sets of applications on a Linux system based on user-defined profiles, thereby streamlining workflows for different tasks.
✨ Key Features: • Create autostart profiles for Linux • Select profiles to launch specific program lists • Personal utility for task-specific program startup • Tested on Fedora 44 KDE
📖 Summary: AutoMagik is a Python application designed to simplify the creation and management of autostart profiles on Linux systems. It allows users to select predefined profiles, each configured to launch a specific list of programs for a particular task, streamlining the startup process for various workflows.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 maltrail | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Network traffic monitoring and detection of malicious infrastructure communication and anomalies.
✨ Key Features: • Comprehensive trail set combining static, public feeds, and custom indicators • Multithreaded Rust sensor with libpcap and optional PACKET_FANOUT • Python server for reporting interface, event intake, and HTTP API
📖 Summary: Maltrail is a network traffic detection system that identifies malicious infrastructure communication and network anomalies by matching observed network data against a set of indicators called 'trails'. It consists of a Rust-based sensor for traffic capture and detection, and a Python server for reporting, event intake, and API access.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 VisoMaster-Fusion | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: AI-powered video face swapping and editing for desktop users.
✨ Key Features: • AI-powered face swapping and editing • Support for images, videos, and live webcam feeds • Multiple swapper models (Inswapper128, InStyleSwapper, SimSwap, etc.) • Multi-face workflows with tracking and similarity thresholding • Face likeness, keypoint replacement, expression editing, and pose controls
📖 Summary: VisoMaster Fusion is a desktop application for AI-powered face swapping, enhancement, and editing across images, videos, and live webcam feeds. It offers a user-friendly graphical interface combined with advanced model controls, batch processing, and GPU acceleration for efficient video manipulation.
